claim.explanation: The Format 2 diagram is garbled. The printed format has a plain first line 'OCCURS integer-1 TO integer-2 TIMES DEPENDING ON data-name-1' and, on a second line, an optional bracket holding the {ASCENDING/DESCENDING} brace followed by 'KEY IS { data-name-2 } ...' (exactly as in Format 1). The markdown merges the two lines: it draws one brace spanning 'integer-1 TO', ASCENDING and DESCENDING (making 'integer-1 TO' read as an alternative of a brace shared with ASCENDING/DESCENDING), and moves the keyword KEY out of the KEY IS phrase to the top right of that brace, leaving the phrase as 'IS { data-name-2 } ...'. The bracket's left edge also falls outside the brace rather than enclosing only the ASCENDING/DESCENDING KEY IS phrase. No choice indicators are printed on this format, so none were lost.
claim.why_it_matters: A grammar or reader working from the markdown would see 'integer-1 TO' as an alternative to ASCENDING/DESCENDING and a KEY-less 'IS { data-name-2 }' phrase, so it could reject the legal source 'OCCURS 1 TO 10 TIMES DEPENDING ON N ASCENDING KEY IS K' or accept malformed variants.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 306 (PDF p328), Format 2: line 1 is the plain 'OCCURS integer-1 TO integer-2 TIMES DEPENDING ON data-name-1' with no brace. Line 2 is the same as Format 1: a bracket that holds a brace stacking ASCENDING over DESCENDING, then 'KEY IS { data-name-2 } ...', the bracket closing, then '... [ INDEXED BY { index-name-1 } ... ]'. No choice-indicator bars are printed. Markdown lines 22-28 draw one tall brace that spans 'integer-1 TO' and ASCENDING/DESCENDING, and they put KEY at the top right of that brace, apart from 'IS { data-name-2 }'. Read literally, this makes 'integer-1 TO' an alternative inside the ASCENDING/DESCENDING brace and moves KEY out of the KEY IS phrase. That changes the syntax the diagram expresses, so it is a normative content defect, not wrapping or layout. Format 1 in the same markdown is rendered correctly, which shows the Format 2 version is a transcription error. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
